title: Hermite coefficient
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\alpha$ assign a nonnegative integer to each coordinate. The Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$ is the integral of $f(x)$ times the Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$, with respect to the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on $\mathbb R^n$
$\alpha$ assigns a natural number to each of the $n$ coordinates
